- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) after a recent rise, model often fails to correct downward; lower forecast by 3–8% for next 3–5 days.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.5.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion after a sharp spike, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5x recent high if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag in direction; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward drift in bearish sentiment; add 2–5% buffer below recent low if sentiment <0.33 for 3+ days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price declines, model overestimates recovery; reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 5 days if sentiment >0.67 but price is falling.
